LOCAL-1.title: Petstore v3 /user [OpGroup]: after a user is created without a username, every lookup of an unknown username answers 500
LOCAL-1.body:
## Error

Once a user without a username exists, every read of a username that does not exist answers `500`
instead of `404`, for every caller, and no API call can remove that record.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /user` with `{}` | no nameless user | `200`, stored with id `0` | `200`, `default` |
| `GET /user/<UNKNOWN_USERNAME>` | after the request above | `500` | `200`, `400`, `404` |
| `GET /user/<UNKNOWN_USERNAME>` | after a service restart | `404` | `200`, `400`, `404` |

Operations covered:

- `POST /user`
- `GET /user/{username}`

## Expected

`POST /user` without a `username` is refused with `400` and stores nothing; a read of an unknown
username answers `404` whatever else is stored. The `500` is ruled out because the request is valid
and the declared answer for a missing user is `404`.

## Suggested fix

Validate `username` as required on create, and make the lookup skip records whose username is
null.

## Reproduce

1. `POST /user` with body `{}`.
2. `GET /user/<UNKNOWN_USERNAME>`: `500`.
3. Only restarting the service brings back `404`.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-10. Measured by an
execution-mode run on data it created (contract note PN-19). Class `broken`: a read the contract
calls valid fails. Severity `S2`: data left unrepairable through the API, affecting every caller.
Cause measured, not read in code.
comments: Supporting detail: the full measurements are in `services/petstore/docs/features/user.md` (Write measurements, contract note PN-19). The record was created by the run itself; recovery needed a service restart.

LOCAL-2.title: Petstore v3 /store [OpGroup]: the inventory answers 500 while any order has no status
LOCAL-2.body:
## Error

While any order without a `status` exists, `GET /store/inventory` answers `500` to every caller.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /store/order` with `{"id": <ORDER_ID>}` | no such order | `200`, stored without `status` | `200`, `400`, `422`, `default` |
| `GET /store/inventory` | after the request above | `500` | `200`, `default` |
| `DELETE /store/order/<ORDER_ID>`, then `GET /store/inventory` | | `200` | `200`, `default` |

A body of `{}` creates such an order with id `0`.

Operations covered:

- `POST /store/order`
- `GET /store/inventory`

## Expected

Either the order is refused because `status` is missing (`400`), or the inventory ignores orders
without a status. A read of the inventory never fails because of one stored order.

## Suggested fix

Give `status` a default or refuse orders without one, and skip null statuses when the inventory
groups orders.

## Reproduce

1. `POST /store/order` with `{"id": <ORDER_ID>}`.
2. `GET /store/inventory`: `500`.
3. `DELETE /store/order/<ORDER_ID>` restores it.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-10. Measured by an
execution-mode run on data it created (contract note PN-17); a sibling with the same shape exists on
`GET /pet/findByTags` (PN-18), with its own code path. Class `broken`: a documented read cannot
succeed. Severity `S2`: one write any caller can send takes a documented operation down for
everyone. Cause measured, not read in code.
comments: Supporting detail: `services/petstore/docs/features/store.md` (Write measurements, contract note PN-17). The sibling on `GET /pet/findByTags` is PN-18 in `services/petstore/docs/features/pet.md`.

LOCAL-3.title: Petstore v3 GET /user/{username} [Endpoint]: any caller reads the stored password
LOCAL-3.body:
## Error

Reading a user returns its stored `password` to any caller, with no credential.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /user/<SEED_USERNAME>` without credentials | seed user | `200`, body with eight fields, `password` included | `200`, `400`, `404` |

Redacted body keys: `id`, `username`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `password` (value masked),
`phone`, `userStatus`.

## Expected

A read never returns a stored credential: `password` is write-only. The schema lists the field,
so this conforms to the document, which is why the document should mark it write-only too.

## Suggested fix

Leave `password` out of every user response and mark it `writeOnly` in the schema.

## Reproduce

1. `GET /user/<SEED_USERNAME>` with no `api_key` header.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-10. Reproduced read-only
(contract note PN-13). Class `exposure`. Severity `S1`: every user's stored credential is readable
by an anonymous caller. Cause measured, not read in code.
comments:
Supporting detail: `services/petstore/docs/features/user.md` (Measurements, contract note PN-13). The value was masked in every record kept.
Re-scoped to [OpGroup] /user: the same serialization returns the stored `password` in write answers too, measured on 2026-10-10 with users the run created.

| Operation | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /user/{username}` | `User` with `password` |
| `POST /user` | the created `User` echoed, `password` included (W-01) |
| `PUT /user/{username}` | the updated `User` echoed, `password` included (W-19) |

Cases citing this key: TC-USER-21, TC-USER-39, TC-USER-56.

LOCAL-4.title: Petstore v3 GET /user/login [Endpoint]: login opens a session for any username and password, or none
LOCAL-4.body:
## Error

`GET /user/login` opens a session for any input: no parameters, an unknown user, or a wrong
password. The declared `400` is never produced.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /user/login` | none | `200`, `Logged in user session: <SESSION>` | `200`, `400` |
| `GET /user/login?username=<UNKNOWN_USERNAME>&password=<PASSWORD>` | user does not exist | `200`, a new session | `200`, `400` |
| `GET /user/login` with a user's right, wrong or no password | user created by the run | identical `200` answers | `200`, `400` |

## Expected

`400` "Invalid username/password supplied" for a missing parameter, an unknown user or a wrong
password; a session only for matching credentials.

## Suggested fix

Check the username and password against the stored user before issuing a session.

## Reproduce

1. `GET /user/login` with no parameters.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-10. Reproduced read-only
and by the execution-mode run (contract note PN-12). Class `access`. Severity `S3`: no operation of
this service checks the session (contract note PN-05), so the bypass grants nothing today; on a
service that honoured sessions it would be `S1`. Cause measured, not read in code.
comments: Supporting detail: `services/petstore/docs/features/user.md` (Measurements and Write measurements, contract note PN-12). The X-Expires-After header is also Java date text, not date-time.

LOCAL-5.title: Petstore v3 /pet [OpGroup]: concurrent pet writes make pet searches answer 500 and can lose a pet that was just created
LOCAL-5.body:
## Error

While requests that change pets run at the same time as other pet requests, a pet search answers
`500`, and a pet that was just created with `200` can be missing from the next read.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /pet/findByStatus?status=sold` | another caller deletes a pet in the same instant | `500` `{"code":500,"message":"There was an error processing your request. It has been logged (ID: <LOG_ID>)"}` | `200`, `400`, `default` |
| `GET /pet/findByTags?tags=<TAG>` | other callers create and delete pets | `500`, or `200` with `[]` for a tag only a just-created pet carries | `200`, `400`, `default` |
| `POST /pet` with a new `<PET_ID>`, then `GET /pet/<PET_ID>` | other callers write pets | `200`, then `404` | `200`, then `200` |

Each request alone answers as declared; the failures need two callers at the same moment.

Operations covered:

- `POST /pet`
- `PUT /pet`
- `POST /pet/{petId}`
- `DELETE /pet/{petId}`
- `GET /pet/{petId}`
- `GET /pet/findByStatus`
- `GET /pet/findByTags`

## Expected

Concurrent requests behave as if they ran one after another: a search answers `200` with the pets
stored at that moment, and a pet created with `200` reads back until it is deleted.

## Suggested fix

`PetData` keeps every pet in one `static List<Pet> pets = new ArrayList<>()` that `addPet`,
`deletePetById` and the searches use without synchronisation. Use a thread-safe store (for example
a `ConcurrentHashMap` keyed by id, or synchronise every access) and let the searches iterate a
snapshot.

## Reproduce

1. Run two callers at once: one repeats `POST /pet` and `DELETE /pet/<PET_ID>` with its own ids,
   the other repeats `GET /pet/findByStatus?status=sold`.
2. Within some hundred iterations the search answers `500`, and occasionally a `GET /pet/<PET_ID>`
   right after its `200` create answers `404`.

## Environment

Local environment and CI, Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-12. Observed by
the e2e runs of the suite (spec files in parallel workers, every case on its own data) and
reproduced locally; contract note PN-26. Class `silent-write`: a create that answered `200` can be
lost. Severity `S2`: one operation quietly loses data with a visible effect on later reads, and the
searches fail for every caller while it happens. Cause read in the code (`PetData.java` at
`swagger-petstore-v3-1.0.28`) and consistent with the access log; the exception itself is not
logged by the image.
comments:
## Evidence

- **CI e2e runs** (each passed on a re-run): pull requests #5 and #15, `TC-PET-60` (`findByTags`
  with the pet's unique tag answered `[]`); #10, `TC-PET-01` (`POST /pet` `200`, then
  `GET /pet/<PET_ID>` `404`); #16, `TC-PET-60` and `TC-PET-63` (`findByTags` answered `500`). The
  seeds are in those runs' logs.
- **Local reproduction:** 12 full runs of `--project=api-petstore` with the default workers gave one
  unexpected result, `TC-PET-55`: `GET /pet/findByStatus?status=sold` answered `500`. The image's
  access log shows, in the same second and right before it, `DELETE /pet/<PET_ID>` `200` from
  another worker, next to `POST /pet` and `PUT /pet` requests.
- **Not a property of one case:** the flake lane (`--repeat-each 6`, 168 executions) was stable;
  the race needs two workers on `/pet` at the same instant.

## Cause in the code

`io/swagger/petstore/data/PetData.java` at tag `swagger-petstore-v3-1.0.28`:

- `private static List<Pet> pets = new ArrayList<>();`, shared by every request;
- `findPetByStatus` and `findPetByTags` iterate it with for-each loops, so a concurrent
  `deletePetById` (`removeIf`) or `addPet` (`remove`, then `add`) makes the iterator throw
  `ConcurrentModificationException`, which the service answers as `500`;
- two `ArrayList.add` calls at once can overwrite one another, which loses a stored pet.

`UserData` and `OrderData` follow the same pattern; they are filed as unconfirmed findings of their
own, because each has its own code to change.

## Test-side mitigation

Until this ships, the Petstore pack runs its cases one worker at a time (`workers` in its
`service.json`), so the suite does not trigger the race on every run. The defect stays recorded
here and in contract note PN-26.

LOCAL-6.title: Petstore v3 /user [OpGroup]: concurrent user writes can lose a user or make user reads answer 500 (unconfirmed)
LOCAL-6.body:
## Error

Unconfirmed finding, read in the code and not reproduced yet: users are kept in one shared list
without synchronisation, so concurrent user writes can lose a user, and a read that iterates the
list while another request changes it can answer `500`.

Operations covered:

- `POST /user`
- `POST /user/createWithList`
- `PUT /user/{username}`
- `DELETE /user/{username}`
- `GET /user/{username}`
- `GET /user/login`

## Expected

Concurrent user requests behave as if they ran one after another.

## Suggested fix

`UserData` keeps users in `private static List<User> users = new ArrayList<>()`; use a thread-safe
store or synchronise every access, as for pets (`LOCAL-5`).

## Reproduce

Not reproduced. To confirm: two callers at once, one creating and deleting users with their own
usernames, the other reading them; look for a `500` on a read or a `404` right after a `200` create.

## Environment

Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-12. Read in `UserData.java` at tag
`swagger-petstore-v3-1.0.28`; same pattern as `LOCAL-5` on pets, with its own code. Proposed class
`silent-write`, severity `S2` once reproduced, by the same criterion as `LOCAL-5`.

LOCAL-7.title: Petstore v3 /store [OpGroup]: concurrent order writes can lose an order or make the inventory answer 500 (unconfirmed)
LOCAL-7.body:
## Error

Unconfirmed finding, read in the code and not reproduced yet: orders are kept in one shared list
without synchronisation, so concurrent order writes can lose an order, and the inventory, which
iterates every order, can answer `500` while another request changes the list.

Operations covered:

- `POST /store/order`
- `DELETE /store/order/{orderId}`
- `GET /store/order/{orderId}`
- `GET /store/inventory`

## Expected

Concurrent order requests behave as if they ran one after another; the inventory answers `200` with
the counts at that moment.

## Suggested fix

`OrderData` keeps orders in `private static List<Order> orders = new ArrayList<>()` and the
inventory iterates it; use a thread-safe store or synchronise every access, as for pets (`LOCAL-5`).

## Reproduce

Not reproduced. To confirm: two callers at once, one placing and deleting orders with their own ids,
the other reading `GET /store/inventory`; look for a `500` from the inventory or a `404` right after
a `200` order.

## Environment

Petstore v3 image `swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`, 2026-10-12. Read in `OrderData.java` at tag
`swagger-petstore-v3-1.0.28`; same pattern as `LOCAL-5` on pets, with its own code. Proposed class
`silent-write`, severity `S2` once reproduced, by the same criterion as `LOCAL-5`.

LOCAL-8.title: Petstore v3 /pet [OpGroup]: writes store pets the contract refuses: no name or photo URLs, a status outside the value set, fields of the wrong type or null
LOCAL-8.body:
## Error

`PUT /pet` and the form update `POST /pet/{petId}` answer `200` and store pets the contract refuses.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PUT /pet` with a stored pet's body, `name` removed | pet `<PET_ID>` with a name | `200`, stored without `name` | `200`, `400`, `404`, `422`, `default` |
| `PUT /pet` with `photoUrls` removed | pet with two photo URLs | `200` | same |
| `PUT /pet` with `status: "<MEMBER>-unknown"` | pet with a valid status | `200`, stored as sent | same |
| `PUT /pet` with `name` a number, `photoUrls` a string or `null`, a `photoUrls` item a number or `null`, `status` a number or `null` | pet `<PET_ID>` | `200` | same |
| `PUT /pet` with `category`, `tags`, `category.id`, `tags[].id`, `category.name` or `tags[].name` `null`, a fraction or a number | pet with a category and a tag | `200` | same |
| `POST /pet/<PET_ID>?name=<NAME>&status=<MEMBER>-unknown` | pet with a valid status | `200`, stored as sent | `200`, `400`, `default` |

Operations covered:

- `POST /pet` (the create stores an out-of-set `status` too, contract note PN-21)
- `PUT /pet`
- `POST /pet/{petId}`

## Expected

`400` with the `{code, message}` input error, and the stored pet unchanged: `name` and `photoUrls`
are required, `status` is limited to `available`, `pending`, `sold`, and each field has a declared
type.

## Suggested fix

Validate the `Pet` body (required fields, the `status` value set, field types) before it is stored,
in the code the create, the update and the form update share.

## Reproduce

1. `POST /pet` with a valid pet `<PET_ID>`.
2. `PUT /pet` with the same body and `status` set to `available-unknown`: `200`.
3. `GET /pet/<PET_ID>`: the stored status is `available-unknown`.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 (`swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`), 2026-10-19. Measured by the spec run
of the Petstore pack on pets it created (TC-PET-30 to TC-PET-34, TC-PET-44), which assert the
refusal and the unchanged state; contract notes PN-06 and PN-21. Class `validation` (stored as sent
but should be refused), with `silent-write` (a numeric `name` is stored as text). Severity `S3`:
wrong data in reads, one resource; no other caller's data and no read is broken. Cause measured, not
read in code.
comments:
Detail from the run of 2026-10-19 (redacted evidence attached to each case's result):

- Of the 11 top-level variants of TC-PET-33, ten answer `200`; `id: null` answers `500` (filed
  separately: a body without an id). Of the nested variants of TC-PET-34, every `null`, fraction and
  wrong-typed value answers `200`; the int64 overflow of `category.id` and `tags[].id` answers `400`
  as expected.
- A pet stored this way no longer matches the `Pet` schema on read (for example `photoUrls: null` or
  `status` outside the value set), so a client that validates responses fails on it.
- The form update with the upper-case form of a member (`SOLD`) is stored as sent too.
- Searches by status kept answering `200` while these pets existed; every case deleted its pet and
  confirmed the delete with a `404` read.

LOCAL-9.title: Petstore v3 /pet [OpGroup]: a pet body without an id answers 500
LOCAL-9.body:
## Error

A pet body without an `id`, or with `id: null`, answers `500` instead of being stored or refused.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PUT /pet` with `{}` | any | `500` `{"code":500,"message":"There was an error processing your request. It has been logged (ID: <LOG_ID>)"}` | `200`, `400`, `404`, `422`, `default` |
| `PUT /pet` with a full pet body and `id: null` | pet `<PET_ID>` | `500`, pet unchanged | same |
| `POST /pet` with a valid pet body without `id` | any | `500`, nothing stored (contract note PN-01) | `200`, `400`, `422`, `default` |

Operations covered:

- `POST /pet`
- `PUT /pet`

## Expected

The create assigns an id (`id` is optional in `Pet`) and answers `200`; the update refuses a body
that names no pet with `400`. Never a `5xx` for a body the client controls.

## Suggested fix

Handle a missing `id` before the store is called: generate one on create, refuse with `400` on
update.

## Reproduce

1. `PUT /pet` with `{}`: `500`.
2. `POST /pet` with `{"name": "<NAME>", "photoUrls": []}`: `500`, and no pet is stored.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 (`swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`), 2026-10-19. Measured by the spec run
of the Petstore pack (TC-PET-39 asserts an input error for `{}`; the `id: null` variant of TC-PET-33);
the create was measured at intake (contract note PN-01). Class `broken`: a valid create without an id
cannot succeed, with `validation` for the update's status code. Severity `S3`: a valid request
fails, and clients route around it by sending an id. Cause measured, not read in code.

LOCAL-10.title: Petstore v3 POST /pet/{petId} [Endpoint]: a form update without name is refused, and one without status removes the pet's status
LOCAL-10.body:
## Error

The form update treats `name` as required and `status` as replaced: without `name` it is refused,
and without `status` the pet loses its status.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /pet/<PET_ID>?status=<OTHER_STATUS>` | pet with a name and status | `400` plain text `No Name provided. Try again?`, nothing changed | `200`, `400`, `default` |
| `POST /pet/<PET_ID>?name=<NAME>` | pet with status `pending` | `200`, the pet is stored without `status` | same |
| `POST /pet/<PET_ID>?name=<NAME>&status=<OTHER_STATUS>` | pet with every field | `200`, only `name` and `status` change | same |

## Expected

Both query parameters are optional. A request with only `status` changes the status and keeps the
name; a request with only `name` changes the name and keeps the status.

## Suggested fix

Apply each parameter only when it is present, instead of requiring `name` and overwriting `status`
with the absent value.

## Reproduce

1. `POST /pet` with a pet `<PET_ID>` whose status is `pending`.
2. `POST /pet/<PET_ID>?name=<NAME>`: `200`.
3. `GET /pet/<PET_ID>`: the body has no `status`.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 (`swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`), 2026-10-19. Measured by the spec run
of the Petstore pack on pets it created (TC-PET-42 asserts the status-only update, TC-PET-43 that
the status is kept); contract note PN-23. Class `silent-write` (an omitted value is changed), with
`broken` (a valid status-only request is refused). Severity `S2`: one operation quietly loses stored
data with a visible effect. Cause measured, not read in code.
comments:
Detail: the refusal without `name` is plain text outside the `{code, message}` envelope (contract
note PN-08). The same `400` answers a request with no parameter at all. The pet that lost its status
no longer appears in any `findByStatus` search until a later write sets one again, so the damage is
repairable through the API but visible to every reader.

LOCAL-11.title: Petstore v3 POST /pet/{petId}/uploadImage [Endpoint]: an upload answers a Pet instead of an ApiResponse and adds a server temporary-file path to the pet's photo URLs
LOCAL-11.body:
## Error

An image upload answers the whole `Pet` instead of the declared `ApiResponse`, and appends a server
temporary-file path to the pet's `photoUrls`, where every reader of the pet sees it.

| Request | Starting state | Received | Declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /pet/<PET_ID>/uploadImage`, `application/octet-stream`, a small image | pet with two photo URLs | `200` with a `Pet` whose `photoUrls` ends with `/tmp/inflector<DIGITS>.tmp` | `200` `ApiResponse`, `400`, `404`, `default` |
| `GET /pet/<PET_ID>` | after the upload | `200`, `photoUrls` holds the same server path | `200`, `400`, `404`, `default` |

## Expected

`200` with an `ApiResponse` (`code`, `type`, `message`), and no server file-system path in any
answer or stored field. If the upload adds a photo, it is a URL the client can use.

## Suggested fix

Return an `ApiResponse` from the upload handler, and store a public URL (or nothing) instead of the
temporary file's path.

## Reproduce

1. `POST /pet` with a pet `<PET_ID>`.
2. `POST /pet/<PET_ID>/uploadImage` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and any bytes.
3. `GET /pet/<PET_ID>`: `photoUrls` includes `/tmp/inflector<DIGITS>.tmp`.

## Environment

Local environment, Petstore v3 (`swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.28`), 2026-10-19. Measured by the spec run
of the Petstore pack on pets it created (TC-PET-47 asserts an `ApiResponse` and the other fields
kept, TC-PET-52 that no server path is exposed); contract note PN-24. Class `exposure` (an internal
path reaches every caller), with `contract` and `silent-write`. Severity `S3`: the path is stored
and served to unauthenticated readers, but it reveals only a temporary-file name. Cause measured,
not read in code.
comments:
Detail: every other field of the pet is kept, and the photo URLs present before the upload stay
(TC-PET-47's state check passes apart from the answer's shape). Each upload appends one more path.
`additionalMetadata` is visible nowhere. An upload without a body answers `400` `No file uploaded`,
a `text/plain` upload `415`, and an unknown pet `404`; those are covered by other cases and are not
part of this issue.
